subject: Re: Sporadic I/O errors during nightly batch inference - triage/closure
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@nimbushealth.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Sporadic I/O errors during nightly batch inference

Hi Neha,

We started seeing intermittent I/O errors in our nightly batch jobs that call Redwood's batch inference endpoint (batch-v2). Errors are sporadic — about 2-3 failures per 5000 requests between 15:30-16:00 PDT on 2026-06-28. The client-side error is "EIO: short write" and our trace ids are: trace-20260628-1532 and trace-20260628-1535.

We haven't changed our integration. This is impacting a small percentage of patient record inference runs; visible in our retry metrics. Can you confirm if there was any degradation or throttling on Redwood's side?

I've attached the client request logs (small snippets) and a sample payload. Let me know if you need more.

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Senior SRE, Nimbus Health
alex.turner@nimbushealth.com

Hi Alex — thanks for the quick report and the logs. We're taking a look now. A couple of quick asks to help triage:

- Can you confirm whether your integration is calling hosted/redwood-dedicated endpoints for this account? (We believe NIM is on Dedicated but want to be sure.)
- Please forward a full server-side request/response pair for one failed trace id (headers + body) if available.
- If possible, include the client-side retry behavior (are you retrying immediately or with backoff?).

Initial checks: we don't see broad-region degradations in our monitoring during the 15:30-16:00 PDT window for the serving fleet that hosts your model. No elevated 5xx rates across the fleet and kernel-level GPU metrics look stable for the Candidate pool.

We'll instrument a deeper trace for the trace ids you listed and compare request timelines to infra events. Rishi, can you pick this up and run a head-to-head against the trace index? Grace, please watch for any related alerts on the dedicated pool.

Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

Hi Neha / team,

Thanks — attached is the full trace bundle for trace-20260628-1532 (HTTP headers + client socket errors). Our infra team reports that the failures are visible on the Nimbus side as socket write errors immediately after sending the request body. We're using a short default timeout + immediate retry.

What we observed: the first attempt for that trace succeeded for 98% of requests; the failing requests show a TLS write error on the client with no obvious 5xx from the server. We do see a spike in our EBS throughput at the same time window, but it's too early to say whether that's causal.

Attaching: trace_20260628-1532.pdf (6 pages, includes timestamps), and extra log lines inlined at the bottom of the PDF.

If you can run a server-side packet/timings diff for that trace id it would be great.

– Alex

Date: 2026-06-30T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sporadic I/O errors during nightly batch inference - triage/closure

Hi Alex — thanks for the trace bundle and for the patience while we investigated. Summary of our findings and next steps below.

What we checked (server side)
- Correlated the provided trace ids with Redwood ingress and egress logs; request arrival times and full request bodies are present on our side for the provided traces. No 5xx or internal service exceptions were logged for those request windows.
- End-to-end TCP/TLS session teardown looks clean in our logs; the last server-side log for trace-20260628-1532 is the 200 response write finishing.
- No matching region/global capacity events or autoscaler activity during the window; no GPU OOMs or kernel errors.

What we observed- The server successfully acknowledged and completed the response within the normal latency envelope. The client-side artifacts you shared show a socket write/close on the client shortly after receiving the response bytes (TLS write failures). There is a correlation with a spike in customer-side EBS throughput that lines up with the timestamps you shared.

Conclusion- Based on the evidence available to Redwood, we could not reproduce a server-side error and did not find service-side errors associated with the traces you supplied. The most likely explanation is a transient client-side/network/storage interaction (e.g., client socket buffer exhaustion due to local I/O saturation) coincident with the same time window.

Next steps / recommended remediation- We propose the following actions:
  1) Nimbus to capture a full tcpdump around the next incident window (we can provide a short tcpdump playbook and filters).
  2) Temporarily increase client-side write timeout and add exponential backoff for the retry to reduce pile-up on transient storage stalls.
  3) If the issue recurs, enable our joint packet-trace session (we can provision a debug session on the dedicated pool and coordinate times).

We consider this thread closed on Redwood's side for server-side faults, but we're happy to collaborate on the above steps and reopen if new evidence points to a service regression. Linking a short internal note we created for this triage: https://redwood.example.com/logs/trace/20260628/1532

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute joint troubleshooting call this week to walk through tcpdump filters and the recommended client changes. Please let us know a couple of windows that work for you.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
